research_basis.authoring_method: Original synthesis using the user brief and the THE DMI implementation reference as the structural benchmark.

objects.focus_statement: At the Novice level, the learner recognises and follows AI-related decisions in understanding how AI works at a usable conceptual level and can demonstrate this in authentic tasks.
observable_behaviours: Recognises when AI Fundamentals matters in familiar tasks and can name basic issues or concepts.
Uses provided examples, prompts, or checklists to make an initial decision in ai fundamentals.
Can give a simple explanation of choices in ai fundamentals, but usually needs support to go beyond the obvious case.

common_misconceptions.statement: thinking AI 'understands' in the same way people do
treating all AI tools as if they use the same data and methods
Overstates competence because the task felt familiar.

role.how_it_changes_observation: AI Fundamentals shows up differently across roles, so evidence should be taken from authentic decisions and artefacts rather than generic self-description.
role.calibration_rule: Use role-relevant examples but do not lower the core standard.

subject_area.how_it_changes_observation: The language, examples, and stakes for AI Fundamentals vary by discipline, especially where methods, evidence norms, or safety expectations differ.
subject_area.calibration_rule: Adapt examples and cases to the field while preserving the same level logic.

prior_ai_experience.how_it_changes_observation: Prior familiarity can change confidence and speed in AI Fundamentals, but confidence alone should not be treated as competence.
prior_ai_experience.calibration_rule: Look for decision quality and transfer, not just fluency or enthusiasm.
